messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: High rate of CUDA OOMs on runtime-prod-us-west-2 (service: inference-runtime) — 120 OOM errors in 5m. Auto-mitigation attempted: sparepool reclaim. Headroom metric per node shows ~12-18% free (nvml), but allocator reports fragmentation. Incident created 1849991234

sam: oncall here, ack. looking at logs now. paging maya + eng-runtime

maya: on my way, pulling last 10m of node logs. any customer impact yet?

sam: yes, we're seeing elevated 5xx for some model variants. tracing shows failed token generation calls with CUDA OOM. frontend retries seeing 502s -> 504s for long prompts. customers: batch-ingest-prod and search-autosuggest-2 reported spikes.

jon: adding context — recent rollout yesterday changed default KV cache reservation from 1GB to 1.5GB when sequence_len>1024. could be related.

ashley: @sam can you paste the allocator vs nvml snapshot? I want to see reserved blocks vs free.

sam: paste below (sanitized):

```
# nvml-smi snapshot (node gpu0)
GPU 0: 81% used (10.4GB / 12.8GB)
Processes: inference-runtime (pid 1234) memory 9.6GB

# runtime allocator view (same container)
Allocator reserved: 12.8GB
Allocator in-use: 11.1GB
Allocator free-but-fragmented: 1.7GB
Reported headroom (allocator): 0.0GB
Runtime sparepool: 256MB free
```

sam: so nvml shows ~1.2GB free, allocator says free fragmented blocks but headroom 0 — allocator refusing new large contiguous allocs.

kevin: that matches a fragmentation scenario. odd because we have configured min-contig-reserve=1GB. maybe cached KV shards holding many small allocations preventing coalescing.

maya: can we trigger compaction in-place or force eviction of KV cache for a subset of models? I can push a canary to reduce KV-reserve on a subset.

jon: pushing policy change now: reduce KV cache reserve for model-x to 256MB on 10% of nodes and redirect canary traffic. rollout command:

```
# rollout canary
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/policies/rollout -d '{"policy":"kv_reserve","model":"model-x","value":"256MB","pct":10}'
```

sam: doing immediate mitigation too — draining one affected GPU node to free contiguous memory and evicting low-priority containers. running:

```
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl delete pod -l job=low-priority-worker -n infra
```

ashley: FYI support: I DM'd accounts team about customers seeing higher latency and some 5xx. created support ticket #INC-4821 and labeled P1-impact.

support-bot: Ticket INC-4821 created. Customers impacted: batch-ingest-prod (20% error rate), search-autosuggest-2 (12% error rate). Escalation email queued.

maya: noticed allocator logs with repeated calls failing on large contiguous allocate: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: allocation failed at 3.1GB contiguous request" — but there are tiny free slabs scattered. fragmentation pattern: many small freed KV blocks but large allocations for attention cache failing.

sam: good catch. hypothesis: reserved blocks (reserved GPU memory held for alignment/quantized kernels) + long-lived KV cache fragments -> contiguous allocation fails even though aggregated free > request.

jon: we can try two live strategies:
1) Reduce per-request max generation length to avoid large allocate spikes (hotfix cfg).
2) Perform runtime compaction: trigger restart of allocator process in-place (graceful restart) which drops non-essential caches.

kevin: (notes) compaction via restart will cause short 200-400ms cold-start for some models; acceptable for canary but could spike error rate.

sam: applied shorter-max-tokens hotfix for model-x and model-y via runtime route override:

```
# route override
POST /routes/model-x/override {"max_tokens":512}
```

ashley: support update posted to customers: "We're investigating elevated 5xx for long-running requests, mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15m." :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

15m later —

sam: canary kv-reserve reduction showing 70% drop in OOMs on canary nodes. draining node-17 freed big contiguous region and pods came up on spare nodes.

maya: NVML vs allocator after compaction attempt on node-17:

```
NVML: GPU 0: 48% used (6.1GB / 12.8GB)
Allocator: reserved 8.0GB, in-use 5.9GB, free-contiguous 2.1GB, sparepool 1.2GB
```

sam: good. errors down 85% cluster-wide after rolling kv reserve to 30% of nodes. 5xx back to baseline for most traffic, batch-ingest-prod still has intermittent failures — its traffic is heavier on older nodes (node-pool legacy-1) which have worse fragmentation.

jon: proposing to increase min-contig-reserve to 1.5GB cluster-wide and gradually trigger drain-restarts on legacy-1 pool. downside: risk of reduced concurrency and some increased cost.

kevin: alternative: enable per-process tlmalloc-like compaction if supported by allocator (not in prod build). risky.

sam: making decision: roll min-contig-reserve -> 1.5GB (gradual) and schedule forced rolling restart of legacy-1 nodes over next 30m. Also create temporary traffic steering away from legacy-1 for heavy long prompts.

ashley: notified Customer Success to communicate to the impacted customers about mitigation plan and ETA.

support-bot: Next update scheduled in 20 minutes. Ticket INC-4821 updated: mitigation rolling, risk of brief interruption during restarts.

20m later —

maya: legacy-1 rolling restart 50% done. OOMs trending down. batch-ingest-prod errors at 3% (within SLO) and search-autosuggest at 1%.

sam: starting post-mortem notes capture: possible root causes:
- KV cache reserve change increased fragmentation for long-running containers
- Allocator fragmentation + reserved blocks prevented large contiguous allocations
- NVML aggregated free memory metric is misleading for contiguous allocation needs

jon: action items assigned:
- revert KV reserve default to 1GB for models > seq_len 1024 (P0) — owner: jon, ETA: 2h
- add allocator-level contiguous-free metric to per-node dashboards (P1) — owner: kevin, ETA: 3d
- implement runtime compaction API to allow in-place coalescing without restart (P2) — owner: eng-runtime, ETA: 2w
- enhance canary rollout checks to include fragmentation heuristics (P1) — owner: maya, ETA: 5d

maya: handing off to next oncall: @maya -> @jon. Jon you're on for followups. please keep INC-4821 updated.

jon: taking over. I'll run through the assigned items and schedule a deeper postmortem. thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4821 resolved at 1849995620. Total duration ~73m. Summary: CUDA OOMs caused by allocator fragmentation despite NVML headroom; mitigations: KV reserve canary/revert, drain/restart of legacy nodes, route overrides, min-contig-reserve bump. Postmortem and RCA to follow. :white_check_mark:

sam: great work team. retrospective follow-up meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00am. :thumbsup:
